name: Sun-wetted air scrubber
subtitle: glass panels that pull CO2 from the wind

effects.effect: sunlight makes a coated surface so water-loving that water spreads flat
an alkaline liquid soaks up carbon dioxide, and lime pulls it back out

effect: sunlight makes a coated surface so water-loving that water spreads flat
how: Machines that pull carbon dioxide out of the air need a huge wet surface for the air to touch, and pumping liquid over plastic packing, which never wets evenly, costs much of their energy. Here tall glass panels carry a coating that sunlight makes so water-loving that a slow trickle of alkaline water spreads into a thin, even film. The wind blows past, the film soaks up carbon dioxide, and lime in a tank at the bottom pulls it back out for storage.
obstacle: The coating loses its water-loving state after dark and under dust, and the film has to stay unbroken across square kilometres of glass.
why: Self-wetting glass is a shipping product; using it as a carbon-capture contactor is new.
real: Searched photocatalytic superhydrophilic glass as a falling-film DAC contactor; found only separate superhydrophilic-glass patents and structured-packing DAC contactors.
